reason: Both opened safely and sensibly with filter and spray-arm checks, but Conversation 1 reached the correct diagnosis (clogged filter plus blocked upper-arm jets) efficiently in three turns and left the homeowner with an honest 'this should fix it' plus a sensible fallback about hard water. Conversation 2 fixated on the slightly stiff upper arm, drifted toward a 'spray arm bearing' fault, and pushed for a model number to find a replacement part twice, even re-showing the part panel after the homeowner said they just wanted to clean it, which is an unjustified part steer per the ground truth. Neither conversation raised the quick-wash programme, salt/rinse aid, or scraping plates, so Conversation 1 wins on honesty and restraint rather than on completeness.
